title: Louis Metcalf's lyrics and the family feeling in Russell's band
summary: Metcalf and Teddy Hill clowned on the stand and Holmes says the band was like a family.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: And this is when Red Allen came into the Band, too?

No. Louis Metcalf was there. That's when we got all the numbers, 'You might get better, you never get well'" -- that's Metcalf's lyrics. It might be his number, I don't know. He was always singing, 'You might get better,

but you'll never get well." He could come up with, you know, some classy things. Just like this: "Take off your can; here come the garbageman." That was in "The Call of the (?)." All them kind of things. He'd sit up there, he'd have a ball on the stand! And the (?)... Him and Teddy Hill, boy! Ha-ha, they'd always be on one another, you know, kiddin' and carryin' on. And there was always something to look forward to. But I didn't play with any of them. I didn't kid or carry on.
But you really enjoyed this band.
Oh, I enjoyed it. It was just like a family. Just like a family, believe me.
Well, I once cornered Al Nicholas about the Russell band, and he said, "We all played the same music. We all had a good time."
